promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority and edit target: keep every piece where and how big it is
Image 2: Finish reference only, a Tri-Tachyon warship hull: matte faceted ceramic armour plates with dark seams. Take its material and restraint; ignore its glowing lines, its beams, the black space and the perspective; not layout

Use case: sketch-to-render, game sprite sheet. Image 1 is the authoritative geometry guide and edit target. Image 2 is a FINISH REFERENCE ONLY, a warship hull: take its matte ceramic armour plate, dark seams and restraint; do not copy its layout, shapes, glowing lines, beams, perspective or black background. Reskin the guide into finished painted game sprites, preserving every shape, band, tone relationship and position, the exact 1536x1024 canvas and all empty space. Do not move, rescale, rotate, merge or add pieces. The sheet holds three separate groups. GROUP 1, THE PLATE (the 960x960 block at x 0-959, y 32-991): ONE continuous picture, five by five cells of 192px, with no gaps, gutters, cell borders, seams, frames or margin, painted in one pass. It is a square raised parapet seen from directly overhead, a closed square ring round a flat 3x3 gun platform (the 576x576 centre). The ring is the guide's band, about 88 pixels INSIDE the plate's outer edge: from the platform outward a narrow sloped inner face, a lighter flat top face, then a dark narrow outer face, exactly as the guide's bands run, mitred at the four corners. Outside the band, the outer 88 pixels of the plate all round are FLAT hard-standing of the same material as the platform inside: keep that flat margin, never extend the parapet to the plate's edge. The parapet's profile and texture must be identical along every side and into every corner so any single cell can be cut out and set against another of its kind with no visible seam. GROUP 2, THE BARRICADE RING (x 992-1519, y 32-559): a low free-standing barricade, a band about 72 pixels wide running round the OUTSIDE border of that square, with a sloped outer face, a flat top and a short inner face as the guide shades them. The middle of the square is EMPTY and fully transparent. Same build all the way round, so any 176-pixel cell of it can be cut out and joined to another. GROUP 3, THE WALL TILES (sixteen separate 84x84 squares in a 4x4 grid at x 1014-1385, y 642-1013): the flat top of a thick defensive wall seen from above, one tile per square. Each tile is a flat wall cap. A tile has a raised rim ONLY along the edges where the guide shows a lighter or darker strip; along every other edge the flat cap runs straight to the tile's edge with NO rim, bevel, border, shadow or darkening, because those edges join the next wall tile seamlessly. Several tiles have no rim at all and are a plain flat cap edge to edge. Keep each tile's strips exactly where the guide has them. Material and style: Tri-Tachyon high-tech deployed kit, field-emplaced armour: modular slabs of MATTE off-white and pale warm-grey ceramic composite armour plate, the same stuff as a Tri-Tachyon warship's hull, with faceted chamfered edges, crisp dark recessed panel seams dividing each slab into large plates, a faint coarse hexagonal ceramic tiling on the plate faces, slight dust and scuffing and a few scorch marks; the slabs stand in dark graphite frames with hinge brackets, locking clamps and short anchor feet where they were set down. Accents are restrained: a thin muted slate-blue stripe or small unit stencil block on some plates and tiny dim status pips, nothing more. NO glow, NO light lines, NO translucent or hard-light panes, NO bright cyan or electric blue, no energy effects: every surface is solid matte ceramic or graphite. The parapet a ring of chamfered ceramic armour slabs in graphite frames on a pale composite deck pad, the wall caps the tops of tall ceramic armour slabs, the barricade a run of low chamfered ceramic slabs on graphite feet. Straight 90-degree overhead orthographic camera, top-down like a strategy-game map sprite, no perspective tilt. Sun from the upper left: keep the guide's lit and shaded faces exactly where they are. Hand-painted gritty science-fiction game-sprite look like Starsector, restrained palette, coarse readable detail that survives being shrunk to about 32 to 64 pixels per cell. No text, no letters, no numbers, no labels, no watermark, no UI, no grass, no extra objects, no cast shadow outside the pieces, no border. True transparent background outside every piece and inside the barricade ring (if transparency is impossible, a flat pure white background). Change only material, surface detail and subtle shading, never placement, size or silhouette.
